title: IQM Quantum Computers Reports First Earnings as Public Company: H1 2026 Results, Record Backlog, and FY 2026 Guidance - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IQM Quantum Computers, newly dual-listed on Nasdaq and Nasdaq Helsinki as Europe's first pure-play quantum computing public company, posted H1 2026 revenue of €8.87M (+47% YoY) against a €74.90M net loss, but backed a €42-47M FY 2026 revenue target on the back of an order backlog that jumped from €69.1M at quarter-end to over €102.1M after a €33.0M CSC/LUMI AI Factory contract. Post-SPAC cash of €309.4M funds a runway into Q2 2028 and a >€40M Espoo fab expansion to double cleanroom capacity to 30 systems per year.

insights.claim: IQM Quantum Computers guided FY 2026 revenue to €42-47 million after generating only €8.87 million in H1 2026, implying roughly 80% of the full-year target must be recognized in the second half.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The guidance is a step-function bet on H2 deliveries and customer acceptances — the single most falsifiable number to track at Q3 print.
insights.quote: FY 2026 Revenue Target: €42 million to €47 million (supported by scheduled delivery and customer acceptance milestones of its initial 150-qubit system).

insights.claim: IQM's FY 2026 revenue recognition hinges specifically on scheduled delivery and customer acceptance milestones of its initial 150-qubit system, making a single machine's acceptance the pivot for the year.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Concentration risk: a slipped acceptance on one flagship system can miss the whole year's guide, a classic capital-equipment revenue timing trap.

insights.claim: IQM's order backlog rose from €69.1 million at June 30, 2026 to more than €102.1 million by August 3, 2026 — a ~48% increase in roughly five weeks driven by one contract.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Backlog, not revenue, is the leading indicator here; a >€100M book against a €42-47M revenue guide sets up multi-year visibility if conversion holds.
insights.quote: elevating total order backlog past €102.1 million as of August 3, 2026

insights.claim: IQM set an FY 2026 order intake target of €65-75 million, below the €33.0 million single CSC award plus the €69.1 million backlog already on the books, signaling management expects lumpy rather than compounding bookings.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Watch whether intake guidance is sandbagged — one more sovereign-scale deal would blow through the top end and reset the multiple.
insights.quote: FY 2026 Order Intake Target: €65 million to €75 million.

insights.claim: A single €33.0 million CSC contract to integrate a quantum computer into the LUMI AI Factory represents roughly a third of IQM's entire order backlog, showing quantum procurement is currently driven by a handful of state-backed HPC centers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Demand is sovereign-compute budget demand, not commercial enterprise demand — track European AI-factory and HPC appropriations as the real revenue driver.
insights.quote: IQM secured a landmark €33.0 million contract with CSC to integrate a quantum computer into the LUMI AI Factory

insights.claim: IQM's H1 2026 operating expenses grew 92.4% year-over-year to €67.30 million while revenue grew only 47%, meaning cost growth is running at roughly double the rate of top-line growth.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Negative operating leverage at this stage means the equity story is entirely about backlog conversion, not margin trajectory.

insights.claim: IQM's H1 2026 net loss of €74.90 million was inflated by non-cash items including a €9.0 million fair-value adjustment on the Aalto University convertible loan conversion feature and revaluation/extinguishment of Kreos Capital loan warrants.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Headline net loss overstates cash burn; the €60.54M operating loss is the cleaner burn proxy for modelling runway.
insights.locator: Net loss for H1 2026 stood at

insights.claim: IQM's SPAC business combination with Real Asset Acquisition Corp. and concurrent PIPE lifted cash from €118.88 million at June 30 to €309.4 million by July 2, 2026, funding a stated runway into Q2 2028.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Roughly two years of funded runway means no near-term dilution overhang, but also sets a hard 2028 deadline to prove commercial traction.
insights.quote: IQM’s cash balance stood at €309.4 million ($337.2M USD), establishing a runway into Q2 2028.

insights.claim: IQM's cash and short-term investments fell 19.4% from €147.42 million at December 31, 2025 to €118.88 million at June 30, 2026, an implied pre-listing burn of roughly €28.5 million in six months.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Compare that historical burn to the new €40M+ fab commitment — capex is about to step up materially against the 2028 runway.

insights.claim: IQM booked €9.9 million of transaction costs on its SPAC business combination and dual listing, a one-off that accounts for roughly a third of the year-over-year widening in H1 operating loss.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Normalizing for this, H2 opex should decelerate — a modelling adjustment most first-look screens will miss.

insights.claim: IQM fully prepaid and terminated its €5.0 million Kreos Capital term loan in July 2026, leaving the balance sheet debt-free immediately after listing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A debt-free, €309M-cash balance sheet removes covenant and refinancing risk from the story entirely.
insights.quote: IQM fully prepaid and terminated its €5.0 million Kreos Capital term loan facility, removing debt obligations from its balance sheet.

themes.theme: Vertically integrated fab as the moat

insights.claim: IQM is committing over €40 million to double cleanroom capacity at its proprietary Espoo, Finland fabrication facility to enable production of up to 30 full-stack quantum computers annually.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Owning the fab is the differentiator versus cloud-only quantum peers; 30 units/year is the capacity ceiling to model against any bull case.
insights.quote: The investment will double cleanroom capacity to enable the production of up to 30 full-stack quantum computers annually.

insights.claim: IQM has sold 26 full-stack quantum computers to date but delivered only 17, leaving a nine-unit delivery gap that maps directly onto the backlog awaiting revenue recognition.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Sold-versus-delivered is the cleanest unit-economics tracker for this name; closing the gap is what converts backlog to revenue.
insights.quote: To date, IQM has sold 26 full-stack quantum computers and delivered 17 globally.

insights.claim: Planned annual capacity of 30 systems dwarfs IQM's cumulative 26 lifetime sales, indicating management is building for a demand inflection that has not yet appeared in bookings.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Either the demand curve steepens sharply or IQM carries expensive idle fab capacity — a binary worth sizing before the 2028 runway expires.

insights.claim: IQM completed its first US delivery in June 2026, shipping to the US Department of Energy's Oak Ridge National Laboratory in Tennessee, breaking into the American national-lab market as a European vendor.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: An ORNL reference customer is the credential that unlocks further DOE and US federal procurement — watch for follow-on US awards as the validation signal.
insights.quote: the company completed its first US delivery to the US Department of Energy’s Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) in Tennessee in June 2026

insights.claim: IQM's dual listing on Nasdaq and Nasdaq Helsinki under ticker IQMX makes it the first European pure-play quantum computing company on Nasdaq, giving US investors a direct European quantum vehicle.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Creates a new comparable in the listed quantum basket and a likely index-inclusion and passive-flow catalyst distinct from US-domiciled peers.
insights.quote: the first European pure-play quantum computing company on Nasdaq and Nasdaq Helsinki

insights.claim: IQM partnered with NVIDIA to use the NVIDIA Ising model family for AI-driven parallel qubit calibration, applying AI to compress the operational bottleneck of tuning quantum hardware.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Calibration time is a hidden cost driver in quantum system delivery; AI-accelerated calibration is a lever on both gross margin and units shipped per year.
insights.quote: Partnered with NVIDIA for AI-driven parallel qubit calibration using the NVIDIA Ising model family

insights.claim: IQM is collaborating with HPE to integrate its quantum systems into HPE Cray HPC infrastructure, positioning quantum as an accelerator inside existing supercomputers rather than a standalone platform.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The QPU-as-HPC-accelerator model is the go-to-market that actually has budget today — it routes quantum spend through existing supercomputing procurement lines.

insights.claim: IQM acquired selected technology assets of Berlin-based Quantistry GmbH for €1.9 million on July 1, 2026 to build a cloud-based, AI-enabled chemical and materials simulation stack.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A cheap tuck-in signals a move up-stack toward application software and recurring revenue, away from pure hardware unit sales.

insights.claim: IQM introduced 'barbell codes', a new family of quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (qLDPC) error correction codes tailored specifically to its own Constellation topology.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Co-designing error-correction codes with hardware topology is how superconducting vendors cut physical-qubit overhead — a technical moat proxy versus competing modalities.
insights.quote: Introduced “barbell codes”—a novel family of quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (qLDPC) error correction codes tailored for the IQM Constellation topology.

insights.claim: IQM's H1 2026 gross profit rose 49.7% to €3.60 million on €8.87 million of revenue, holding gross margin near 41% even as the revenue mix shifted toward standardized on-premises systems.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Stable ~40% gross margin through a 47% revenue ramp suggests the standardized-system product is not margin-dilutive as volume scales.

insights.claim: IQM's revenue growth is driven by two distinct engines — delivery of standardized on-premises quantum systems and milestone progress on customized long-term projects — which have different recognition timing and margin profiles.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Model the two streams separately: standardized units are lumpy at delivery, custom projects accrue on milestones, and the blend explains quarterly volatility.
insights.quote: driven primarily by the delivery of standardized on-premises quantum computing systems and milestone progress on customized long-term projects

insights.claim: IQM grew R&D spend to €34.05 million in H1 2026 from €25.65 million a year earlier and scaled to 460 employees globally, with R&D alone running roughly four times H1 revenue.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: R&D at 4x revenue is the defining economics of pre-commercial quantum — the listed peer set should be screened on this ratio, not on P/E.

insights.claim: The article's own figures are internally inconsistent on the USD conversion of H1 2026 revenue, citing $10.20 million in the summary table but $9.67 million in the narrative for the same €8.87 million.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Use the reported euro figures, not the USD translations, when building comparables against US-listed quantum peers.
